subject: astronomy
title: Solar System Foundations
welcome_lead: Tour the eight planets, the dwarf worlds, and the icy frontier of our cosmic neighbourhood.
meta_desc: GCSE Astronomy: planets, dwarf planets, asteroid belt, Kuiper belt, Oort cloud and recent missions.
final_note: You now know the layout of the Solar System from Mercury to the Oort cloud.

walkthroughs.body_html: From the Sun outward: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars (rocky terrestrials), then Jupiter, Saturn (gas giants) and Uranus, Neptune (ice giants). The asteroid belt sits between Mars and Jupiter.
Pluto (Kuiper belt), Eris (scattered disc) and Ceres (in the asteroid belt) are dwarf planets. They are round but have not cleared their orbital path of other debris.
Voyager 1 (1977) crossed the heliopause in 2012. Parker Solar Probe (2018) studies the Sun's corona. Perseverance landed on Mars in 2021. JWST launched December 2021.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a solar eclipse and a lunar eclipse?
